newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Issing says inflation not defeated yet.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing says inflation not defeated yet.

text.p: Despite signs to the contrary, inflationary dangers have not been permanently defeated, Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Friday.
"The danger of inflation is not dead simply because current statistics testify to price stability," Issing said in a speech prepared for delivery at a forum held outside of Frankfurt.
A copy of the speech, written in English, was made available beforehand.
Issing added he did not want to join a growing chorus of economists who are declaring that inflation has been conquered.
Looking ahead Issing said "the fight against inflation will not have been won definitely until inflation has disappeared once and for all from the range of policy options."

To root out inflationary dangers, central banks must be independent, solely committed to price stability and be able to "put this goal into practice by credibly applying their set of instruments," Issing said.
Issing warned that in light of alarmingly high debt levels in some countries, "this will be the only way to prevent renewed considertation being given to inflation tax."
Issing added that at the moment this "seems to be a comfortable option for the government to reduce the burden of its debt but always turns out to be an expensive strategy in economic terms."

In Germany most independent economists forecast inflation rates, currently standing at 1.5 percent in west Germany in October, will rise slightly in coming months but still said this would be no cause for concern.
Separately Issing also said that the successful fight against inflation is "proof of the fact that there is no inherent conflict between the present exchange rate system and stable domestic prices."
